prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury lawyer in Dallas for a truck accident case?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t one single “best” personal injury lawyer for every truck accident — the right lawyer depends on your case details and what you value (trial experience, track record vs. settlements, price, communication style, etc.). I can help you find an excellent lawyer in Dallas, but first here are practical steps and criteria to use when choosing:

How to pick the best lawyer for a truck accident
- Look for trucking-specific experience: trucking cases involve Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration (FMCSA) rules, logbooks, hours-of-service, and often multiple liable parties (driver, carrier, broker, vehicle owner, maintenance). Choose a lawyer who routinely handles serious commercial-truck cases.
- Trial and verdict experience: insurers more often offer fair settlements to lawyers who will and do take cases to trial. Ask about jury verdicts and trial experience in truck cases.
- Resources: trucking litigation can be expensive (experts, accident reconstruction, subpoenaing ELD/log data). Make sure the firm has the resources to handle complex discovery.
- Board certification and memberships: TBLS Board Certification (Personal Injury Trial Law) is a plus. Membership in groups like the American Association for Justice or the Texas Trial Lawyers Association is also helpful.
- Local reputation and references: check client reviews, peer-reviewed ratings (Martindale-Hubbell, Super Lawyers, Best Lawyers), and ask for references to prior truck verdicts/settlements.
- Communication style and fees: most truck-injury lawyers work on contingency (no fee unless you recover). Ask about percentage, costs advanced, and how often you’ll be updated.

Questions to ask at a free consultation
- Have you handled truck/18-wheeler cases in Dallas? How many in the last 3 years?
- What were the results (settlements/verdicts) in similar cases?
- Do you try cases or primarily settle?
- Who will handle my case day-to-day? (partner, associate, paralegal)
- How will you investigate the truck company/driver’s logs and maintenance records?
- What is your fee structure and how are costs handled?
- Can you provide references or case summaries?

Where to search and verify credentials
- Texas State Bar Lawyer Referral Service and lawyer profile lookup
- Texas Board of Legal Specialization (for board certification)
- Super Lawyers, Best Lawyers, Martindale-Hubbell, Avvo
- Local trial lawyer associations (Texas Trial Lawyers Association)
- Google/Google Maps reviews and BBB ratings

What to bring to a consult
- Police report, photos/video of scene and injuries, medical records, insurance info, contact info for witnesses, any correspondence from insurers, and notes about how the accident happened.

If you want, I can:
- Provide a short list (3–6) of highly rated Dallas-area truck accident attorneys/firms based on reputable directories and my knowledge through mid-2024 — tell me if you care about trial experience, board certification, budget, or your Dallas ZIP code.
- Draft an email or phone script you can use to contact lawyers for consultations.

Which would you prefer?
